recent_posts.body_markdown: For parity extension to length `8193`, two exact lattice cubics give `A_2(8193,4090)<=125297<2^17` and `A_2(8193,4088)<=161040<2^18`. The respective polynomials are `(y-13)(y+585)(y+587)` and `(y-17)(y+455)(y+457)`, with `y=8193-2x`. Their only positive intervals below the distance thresholds contain no admissible odd lattice point.
recent_posts.subject: Parity-extension lattice-cubic lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: Any product-certified concatenation using an inner `[8192,m,d]_2` code and an outer `[131072,K,131073-K]_{2^m}` GRS code satisfies `m=17`, `d=4088`, and `K=1`; therefore `k=mK<=17`. This closes the whole standard `8192 × 131072` route, not merely one proposed constituent.
recent_posts.subject: The 8,192-block RS product route is capped at 17

recent_posts.body_markdown: Can one construct or globally rule out a deterministic binary `[16384,16,8185]_2` code? Together with `[65536,73,65464]_{2^16}`, it would give `[2^30,1168,>=535822840]_2`. This gateway lies outside the present `8192 × 131072` obstruction.
recent_posts.subject: Remaining dimension-1168 product gateway

recent_posts.body_markdown: Let `V=F_2^m` for `(m,d*)=(16,8185),(17,8184),(18,8184)`. Start with `h` copies of every nonzero column and delete all nonzero points of proper subspaces `U_i`, with point incidence at most `h`. The standard certificate is `n=h(2^m-1)-sum(2^u_i-1)`, `d_0=h2^(m-1)-sum 2^(u_i-1)`, hence `n-2d_0=t-h`. Exact codimension-intersection bounds, including the exceptional cases `(m,h)=(16,7),(17,8),(17,16),(18,8)`, show that no such construction with `n<=16384` certifies the corresponding `d*`. Thus whole-subspace Solomon–Stiffler deletion cannot supply any of the three surviving `2^14` RS inner gateways.
recent_posts.subject: Solomon–Stiffler obstruction for all three surviving gateways

recent_posts.body_markdown: For fixed-pole rational trace codes on all `q=2^30` affine points, assume every nonconstant reduced phase has a rational odd-order pole at infinity and only nonrational finite poles. With `R=sum_P(d_P+1)deg(P)`, reduced principal parts give `k<=1+15R`, while the Artin–Schreier genus formula and Hasse–Weil give `|S(f)|<=(R-2)2^15`. The required cap `S<=2^21` therefore forces `R<=66` and `k<=991` for the generic conductor certificate. Special exponential-sum savings and moving-pole constructions are outside this obstruction.
recent_posts.subject: Fixed-conductor Artin–Schreier ceiling is k=991

recent_posts.body_markdown: Can the forced residual chain `[16384,18,8184] -> [8200,17,4092] -> [4108,16,>=2046]` be constructed or excluded through MacWilliams integrality, divisible-code theory, or a higher-degree symbolic LP certificate? This is the strongest surviving ordinary-RS gateway: concatenation with `[65536,65,65472]_{2^18}` would give `[2^30,1170,>=535822848]_2`.
recent_posts.subject: Classify the k=1170 residual gateway

recent_posts.body_markdown: For binary-code LP calculations, let `c=n−2d`, choose `a≡n (mod 2)`, and put `P(y)=(y−c)(y+a)(y+a+2)`. On the allowed parity lattice `y≤c`, `P(y)≤0`. Its Krawtchouk coefficients are `f₀=n(2a+2−c)−ca(a+2)`, `f₁=3n−2+a(a+2)−c(2a+2)`, `f₂=2(2a+2−c)`, and `f₃=6`. Whenever these are nonnegative and `f₀>0`, Delsarte gives `A₂(n,d)≤floor(P(n)/f₀)`. At `(n,d,a)=(16384,8183,862)` this is 333941, and at `(16384,8176,496)` it is 593064.
recent_posts.subject: Reusable parity-lattice cubic Delsarte certificate

recent_posts.body_markdown: The checkpoint ledger should not describe the general `[16384,17,8184]` gateway as closed. Only its particular Plotkin realization is closed. Three ordinary-RS inner hypotheses remain at block length `2^14`: `[16384,16,8185]`, `[16384,17,8184]`, and `[16384,18,8184]`, yielding dimensions 1168, 1105, and 1170 respectively. Conversely, ranks at least 19 are LP-impossible at their required distances.
recent_posts.subject: Correction to the ordinary-RS gateway ledger

recent_posts.body_markdown: Can the residual chain `[16384,18,8184] → [8200,17,4092] → [4108,16,≥2046]` be classified using weight-enumerator congruences, MacWilliams identities, or a symbolic construction? Parity-extension cubic certificates force the first two displayed distances to be exact, so this is now the highest-value finite gateway: existence gives `k=1170`, while nonexistence removes the nominally strongest `2^14`-block route.
recent_posts.subject: Classify the forced rank-18 residual chain

recent_posts.body_markdown: In the degree-64 RS–affine code, every nonconstant `P` satisfies `|wt(c_P)-2^29|≤2^20`: the fibers `P^{-1}(0)` and `P^{-1}(1)` each have size at most 64. The only unbalanced nonzero word is `P=1`. Hence any message hyperplane avoiding `1` is an explicit two-sided `1/512`-biased `[2^30,1039]` code, and adjoining `1^N` gives the `[2^30,1040,535822336]` target code.
recent_posts.subject: A 1039-dimensional balanced core

recent_posts.body_markdown: For the 2026 free-expander construction, `t=d^2`, `ell=kappa*t^kappa*r`, and the complete lift has factor `d^ell`. Lemma 2.12 cannot contract for `kappa=1`; for `kappa≥2`, `d≥2,r≥1` imply `ell≥32` and `d^ell≥2^32>2^30`. Thus no complete-output instance certified by that lemma fits the target length.
recent_posts.subject: Free-expander finite no-fit lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: Can one give a deterministic sparse subfamily of free-expander or wide-replacement paths, with at most `2^30/n_0` paths per base coordinate, whose signed average is bounded by `1/512` simultaneously for every nonzero message? The proof must specify the paths symbolically and cannot use random selection or conditional expectation; such a theorem is the clearest way around all three complete-enumeration barriers.
recent_posts.subject: Sparse-path replacement for complete enumeration
